newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's reserves set to increase - report.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's reserves set to increase - report.

text.p: Malaysia's reserves are expected to increase by 19.1 percent to 41.2 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP) by the end of next year if Malaysians ensure the national savings campaign succeeds, a local newspaper reported on Thursday.
The campaign, launched on Monday by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, aims to increase the national savings rate to 45 percent by end-1997 from 38.8 percent of gross national product (GNP).

The Business Times quoted Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim as saying that the higher reserves would enable the government to finance most of its investments, and hence avoid heavy borrowing from foreign sources.

"The country's reserves continue to increase and this has reduced the savings-investment gap. Investment, meanwhile, has strenghtened, reflecting investor confidence in our prudent economic management," Anwar told parliament.
According to the central bank, Bank Negara, Malaysia's reserves stood at 69.6 billion ringgit at the end of November, against 63.8 billion ringgit at end-1995.
Anwar, however, warned that although the country's reserves are quite high, they are not enough to finance heavy investment.
"To reduce foreign financing, the national saving rates need to be improved further," he said. -- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-230 8911)
